Top scalers: the fastest-growing high-growth firms

Source: R/compute-top-scalers.R
compute_top_scalers.Rd

New analysis. Ranks the high-growth scalers of each year by how much they grew over the 3-year window t-3..t and describes the fastest ones, in the format of compute_characteristics().

Usage

compute_top_scalers(
  config,
  accounts_indicators,
  cutoffs = c(top50 = 50, p1 = 0.01, p5 = 0.05, p10 = 0.1, p25 = 0.25),
  joint_growth = FALSE
)

Arguments

config

A scaleup_config from config_scaleup().

accounts_indicators

The output of build_accounts_indicators() (with the trade columns when built with a trade panel: then L3exporter is a breakdown too).

cutoffs

Named cut-offs: values >= 1 are a number of firms, values below 1 a share of the ranked scalers.

joint_growth

If TRUE, rank only scalers whose other variable also grew over t-3..t (turnover for employment scalers, employment for turnover scalers). run_scaler_analysis() reports both versions.

Value

A tibble.

Details

Population. Scalers as in the package, 20 % definition: employment scalers (HGE20) are ranked by employment indices, turnover scalers (HGT20) by turnover indices; firms with 10 to fewer than 250 employees at t-3, from the fourth panel year on (as in compute_characteristics()). Growth driven by an acquisition (acquisition == 1) is excluded; a missing acquisition flag does not exclude the firm.

Indices (x = employment or turnover):

  • rel: relative growth, x / L3x - 1 (same ranking as the CAGR);

  • abs: absolute growth, x - L3x;

  • bs: Birch-Schreyer, (x - L3x) * x / L3x.

Ranking. Within each year (one country per run). Ties on the index are broken by a second, then a third index: rel -> abs -> bs, abs -> rel -> bs, bs -> abs -> rel. Firms still tied share the better rank, so every firm tied at a cut-off is included.

Cut-offs. top50 = rank <= 50; p1, p5, p10, p25 = rank <= the share times the number of ranked scalers that year, rounded up (at least 1). Every cut-off is reported for every cell; nothing is blanked.

Output. One row per (year, sample, category, group). sample is <scaler>_<index>_<cutoff> (e.g. HGE20_rel_p10) or <scaler>_ranked for all ranked scalers. Columns as in compute_characteristics() (firm count, approximate medians, means, ownership shares, optional dominance), plus:

  • n_ranked, rank_cutoff: scalers ranked that year and the rank cut-off;

  • S3pos_employment, S3pos_turnover: the cell's gross 3-year creation (sum of the positive x - L3x);

  • share_creation_employment, share_creation_turnover: that creation over the gross creation of all firms in the same year and group (entrants count with their whole size, as in compute_contribution(); the group is taken at t-3, else at t).
